metas.name: Antofagasta de la Sierra
metas.note:
Where : northern Catamarca, south of Antofagasta de la Sierra, RP43

Description : South starts out as dry and has rocky mountains that are sandy. As the road continues it becomes high altitude and accumulates dark volcanic rock/gravel. The north is particularly distinct with lower clouds.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Catamarca
metas.note: Description : Catamarca has a big ridge east and a big ridge west, with an open valley to the south and hills to the north sometimes visible.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Cerro El Morro
metas.note:
Where : northeastern San Luis, north of Villa Mercedes, around Cerro El Morro

Description : Landscape is quite flat except for a seemingly random mountain in the middle of nowhere which is very distinct.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Cerro Nevado
metas.note:
Where : central Mendoza, south of San Rafael, roads around Cerro Nevado

Description : Very distinct snow-capped ridge can be seen from very far.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Comodoro Rivadavia
metas.note: Description : Comodoro Rivadavia is a very hilly coastal town, surrounded by distinct limestone mountains, the main city is mostly Gen4 and the outskirts mostly Gen3.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Comodoro Rivadavia hills
metas.note:
Where : southeastern Chubut, west of Comodoro Rivadavia

Description : East-west valleys with small hills, green southern vegetation and low sun hidden behind the ridges. Occasionally it can have snow too.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: El Cain
metas.note:
Where : central Rio Negro, around El Cain, RP8 & RP5

Description : overcast gen3 road, winter coverage.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Iruya
metas.note:
Where : northern Salta, south of Iruya, RP133

Description : Very distinct dry mountains with slight pink/tan rock and almost looks as if somebody cut them with a knife or took a bite out.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: La Rioja
metas.note: Description : La Rioja has a very close ridge going north to south to the west, and flatness to the east and the south.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Lago Salinas Grande
metas.note:
Where : southern Catamarca, around the Lago Salinas Grandes, RN60/157

Description : Pinkish brown soil that is dried out and flat with green bushes on either side. Abundance of cacti. Certain areas are quite barren particularly where the map shows water. Road angle is useful to confirm.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Las Leñas
metas.note:
Where : southwestern Mendoza, east of Las Leñas, RP222

Description : Massive front blur and distinct snow poles. The road runs along a dried up river bed with light green vegetation.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Mendoza
metas.note:
Description : Mendoza has very big mountains to the west, with not real elevation to the east. Vineyards and winter coverage are very common.

It is very easy to confuse with San Juan, however a ridge can be seen in the east in San Juan (which is not obvious on every loc, so sending the wrong one is pretty common).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Nazareno
metas.note:
Where : northern Salta, near Nazareno, RP69

Description : Very narrow, dangerous-looking road and high altitude. Looks very similar to some roads seen in Peru.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Parque Nacional Los Cardones
metas.note:
Where : central Salta, around Parque Nacional Los Cardones

Description : Dry open valleys with Cardon cacti spam.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Parque Nacional Talampaya
metas.note:
Where : central La Rioja, around and in Parque Nacional Talampaya, RN76

Description : Very wide open valley with distant reddish mountains and some of the most distinct pink sandy soil in the country.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Posadas
metas.note: Description : Posadas is the biggest town in Misiones, with a very consistent grid going ESE. The town is a bit hilly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Rio Gallegos
metas.note:
Description : Rio Gallegos has a pretty consistent grid and Gen4 snowy coverage in the town.

In Gen3 it is very easy to mistake it for Rio Grande, in Tierra del Fuego.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN101 (paved)
metas.note:
Where : northern Misiones, east of Puerto Iguazú, RN101

Description : Classic misiones brownish road but with danish road lines (outside and inside) between the crossroad with the RN12 and the airport, only place with those road lines in Misiones.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN101 (unpaved)
metas.note:
Where : northern Misiones, east of Puerto Iguazú, RN101

Description : Unpaved E-W road with very overgrown Brazilian looking vegetation. Road is wetter in the west.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN12
metas.note:
Where : northern Corrientes, west of Posadas, RN12

Description : Big tree plantations (sometimes very far), Misiones-looking reddish road (but without a classic Misiones landscape).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN14
metas.note:
Where : eastern Entre Rios, southern Corrientes, RN14

Description : Divided highway until Paso de los Libres (under Uruguaiana label), only highway with this angle in those two provinces, tree plantations, yellow inner line.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN141
metas.note:
Where : eastern San Juan, east of San Juan, RN141

Description : Distinct big flat ridge north that appears to taper at one end. Sometimes a small ridge can be seen far south.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN149
metas.note:
Where : southern San Juan, south of Barreal, RN149

Description : Very open valley, ridges in all directions, paved in the San Juan part, unpaved in Mendoza (the ridges are further away than the RP412 in San Juan). Clouds sit almost only on top of the mountains giving a distinct look.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN150
metas.note:
Where : northern San Juan, west of San José de Jachal, RN150

Description : East to west valley, exposed dark rock is common and sun behind the ridges. Looks vaguely like mountains seen in Oman/UAE, but darker.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN150
metas.note:
Where : western San Juan, west of Las Flores, RN150

Description : East to west valley, exposed dark rocky mountains and melting snow the further west you go.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN151
metas.note:
Where : western La Pampa, south of Santa Isabel, RN151

Description : Very flat, paved road with small bushes, you will always have a power line to the west and the weather is cloudy but not overcast.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN16
metas.note:
Where : eastern Chaco, northwest of Resistencia, RN16

Description : Divided highway, the only one in Chaco, one of the lanes has danish road lines and the road may be a bit reddish.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN226
metas.note:
Where : southeastern Buenos Aires, between Balcarce and Mar del Plata, RN226

Description : Divided road that has tabletop hills with rocky ridge lines just like you will see in Lesotho.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN237
metas.note:
Where : southern Neuquén, south of Villa El Chocón, RN237

Description : Straight road with a lake visible south (most of the time). Has a shorter recognisable ridge north that can be useful if the lake isn't visible.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN251
metas.note:
Where : eastern Río Negro, north of General Conesa, RN251

Description : straight north to south road, danish road lines, sunset coverage, gets worse the further north you go.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN3
metas.note:
Where : eastern Río Negro, east of San Antonio Oeste, RN3

Description : Straight east to west angle, paved road. Powerline north which can help. Bushes might be bigger than expected since it is near the coast. Occasional sand dunes but not as often as the road to Bahia Creek.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN3
metas.note:
Where : southeastern Santa Cruz, west of Rio Gallegos, RN3

Description : East to west divided highway (southernmost in the world) with a small ridge north, overcast, lamps are common throughout this road too.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN3
metas.note:
Where : northeastern Chubut, between Puerto Madryn and Trelew, RN3

Description : Divided road with danish road lines on one lane. Coast is occasionally visible and therefore a good clue.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN3 (paved)
metas.note:
Where : Tierra del Fuego, between San Sebastián and Ushuaia, RN3

Description : Only major paved road in Tierra del Fuego, big mountains on the southern portion, slightly hilly and trees around Tolhuin, mostly overcast.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN3 (unpaved)
metas.note:
Where : southwestern Tierra del Fuego, west of Ushuaia, RN3

Description : Unpaved road, with a few cars passing by usually and a slightly larger road with the Ushuaia mountains visible commonly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN34
metas.note:
Where : northern Salta, north of Tartagal, RN34

Description : Very dry looking with a distinct small ridge west and trafficked. Occasionally pink flower trees can be seen and palms.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN38
metas.note:
Where : central La Rioja, around La Rioja to Catamarca, RN38

Description : Big ridge to the west all the way through, flat to the east except in the northern part near Catamarca.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN40
metas.note:
Where : central La Rioja, west of Nonogasta, RN40

Description : Road running between very red mountains with green bushes covering them. The mountains are not as big as those south of Salta.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN40
metas.note:
Where : western Río Negro, south of San Carlos de Bariloche, RN40

Description : North south valley, with lots of yellow flowers in bushes, sometimes along a lake.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN40
metas.note:
Where : northern Jujuy, east of Ciénaga de Paicone, RN40

Description : Typical dry Jujuy landscape with reddish mountains and driving on the dried up river bed.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN40 (Gen3)
metas.note:
Where : southwestern Jujuy, south of Huáncar, RN40

Description : Only major Gen3 road left in Jujuy, road going through high altitude reddish hills.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN40 in Catamarca
metas.note:
Where : central Catamarca, RN40

Description : Car meta road (for the moment), only major mountainous road in western Argentina to have Striped car.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN52
metas.note:
Where : western Jujuy, around Susques, RN52

Description : Paved road going through high altitude hills and often has pinkish red soil and salt.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN52
metas.note:
Where : central Jujuy, around Santuario de Tres Pozos, RN52

Description : Road going through a salt pan. Very flat with mountains in the distance.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN60
metas.note:
Where : northern Catamarca, south of Las Peladas, RN60

Description : High altitude road that mostly goes through a narrower N-S valley and has salt, crushed volcanic rock and even a volcano visible in the north section.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN68
metas.note:
Where : southern Salta, north of Cafayate, RN68

Description : One of the most beautiful roads in Argentina. Has large exposed red rocky mountains and a dried up river bed visible in some areas.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN7
metas.note:
Where : western San Luis, west of San Luis, RN7

Description : East to west divided highway, with one lane concrete and one lane asphalt, the asphalt lane has danish road lines and lamps are commonly seen in the divide.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN7
metas.note:
Where : northwestern Mendoza, west of Upsallata, RN7

Description : Busy road, you’ll always see cars driving around, E-W valley, incredible mountains and snow coverage visible in the west.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN76
metas.note:
Where : northern La Rioja, north of Jagüé, RN76

Description : Unpaved road, high altitude red sandy hills (and sometimes more white ones). The red sandiness is different from the other high altitude roads mentioned in this guide.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN79
metas.note:
Where : southern Catamarca, around Olta, RN79

Description : SSE ridge, flat to the east, can be mistaken for the road around Villa San Agustin (R2 San Juan) however the ridge is slightly smaller here (here as in on the RN79).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RN86
metas.note:
Where : northern Salta, east of Tartagal, RN86

Description : Very overcast road that is unpaved with brown soil, consistent angle and visible ridge if looking west down the road.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Road to Villa de Merlo
metas.note:
Where : western Córdoba, east of Villa de Merlo

Description : Barren road due to the altitude, has dark rocks and occasional trees and a fence, winter coverage on a hilly plateau.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Roads south of Resistencia
metas.note:
Where : southeastern Chaco, south of Resistencia

Description : Unpaved white sandy roads that are narrow with Caranday wax palms commonly but not always visible.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP1
metas.note:
Where : eastern Río Negro, on the coast east of Pozo Salado, RP1

Description : Road along the coast, water can rarely be seen south, otherwise you’ll be along a dune.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP1
metas.note:
Where : central Neuquén, north of Paso de los Indios, RP1

Description : Very red soil, unique overcast look, landscape going from very flat to hilly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP11
metas.note:
Where : western Santa Cruz, west of El Calafate, RP11

Description : Concrete road wrapping around a mountain, with snow-capped mountains across a lake and snow near the road too.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP119
metas.note:
Where : southern Tierra del Fuego, south of Lago Fagnano, RP119

Description : Road on the side of a hill (hill is south) with occasional water with mountains across it visible north and southern Patagonian forest.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP153
metas.note:
Where : central Mendoza, north of Monte Comán, RP153

Description : Massive front blur, very flat, reddish road and has Mendoza specific pole tops commonly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP173
metas.note:
Where : central Mendoza, southwest of San Rafael, RP173

Description : Massive front blur and road runs in an exposed dry rocky valley but has green vegetation and big trees and is trafficked.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP176
metas.note:
Where : northern Santiago del Estero, south of Nueva Esperanza, RP176

Description : Very straight north south road, paved, can be mistaken with the road south of Monte Quemado (R1 Santiago del Estero) however the grass here (here as in on the RP176) is of a way brighter green (and the car/copyright is different).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP21 & RP19
metas.note:
Where : western Santa Cruz, north of El Calafate, RP21/RP19

Description : Two unpaved roads along a lake either north or south (within Patagonia this configuration is mainly found on those two lakes, with only a few other smaller ones).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP23
metas.note:
Where : central Formosa, south of General Manuel Belgrano, RP23

Description : Very wide unpaved road with Caranday wax palms commonly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP23
metas.note:
Where : western Neuquén, around Rahue, RP23

Description : North to south valley along a river, sometimes the river isn’t visible. Has a lot of trees for being this south in a valley and gen 4 in the north.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP23 & RP11
metas.note:
Where : western Santa Cruz, north of El Calafate, RP23/RP11

Description : Paved roads. The north road in the image can be recognised by the fact that it comes up really close to the mountains and has a lake south. The south road can be recognised because you can see snow-capped mountains across a glacial lake north.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP24 & RP3
metas.note:
Where : western Santiago del Estero, southwest of Santiago del Estero, RP24/RP3

Description : Very low ridge to the west and flatness to the east, the ridge is so small that it might not be visible sometimes.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP3
metas.note:
Where : central San Luis, from Nogolí to San Luis, RP3

Description : Divided by a ditch with curbs and has a rocky ridge to the east.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP30
metas.note:
Where : northern Santa Fe, just south of the border with Chaco, RP30

Description : Very narrow unpaved dirt road, going east to west, grey soil, very flat, sometimes palms can be seen.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP30
metas.note:
Where : eastern Chubut, west of Camarones, RP30

Description : Very snowy road on the west, sunset coverage on the east. The snow covers parts of the road which is different from the road to Fitz Roy.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP307
metas.note:
Where : western Tucuman, around El Mollar, RP307

Description : Tropical looking road, curb with white paint is the best clue to identify this road, trafficked and gets barren in the northern part due to the high altitude however the white painted curbs will still be present.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP33
metas.note:
Where : southern Catamarca, south of Catamarca, RP33

Description : Straight N-S road with an east ridge and has concrete poles on either side of the road. West also has a ridge closer to Catamarca. Gen 3 is very overcast.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP4
metas.note:
Where : central Catamarca, north of Catamarca, RP4

Description : North section is unpaved with pinkish soil and large bulbous green hills visible west. Further south the road is going through a green N-S valley.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP412
metas.note:
Where : western San Juan, north of Calingasta, RP412

Description : Very open valley in gen 3, sunny, small dry bushes, exposed ridges in every direction and is unpaved.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP43
metas.note:
Where : northeastern Santa Cruz, between Pico Truncado and Fitz Roy, RP43

Description : Melting snow on the side of the road, very straight and specific angle, paved. Does not have snow on the actual road but rather around it.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP43
metas.note:
Where : northwestern Santa Cruz, west of Perito Moreno, RP43

Description : Paved road with a dark blue lake north, very green vegetation can be seen as well.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP46
metas.note:
Where : central Catamarca, around Villa de Pomán, RP46

Description : Very large and distinct rocky ridge (larger than other ridges) sometimes very distant mountains visible west and ridge north in the northern section.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP46
metas.note:
Where : central Catamarca, north of Villa de Pomán, RP46

Description : East-west road cupped by mountains all around except south.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP47
metas.note:
Where : central Salta, southeast of Salta, RP47

Description : Pink soil, a portion is along a lake, red to pink exposed rocks with green dry vegetation in the east.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP5
metas.note:
Where : northern Jujuy, on the border with Salta, RP5

Description : High altitude road climbing into the clouds. That’s it.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP51
metas.note:
Where : western Córdoba, north of Villa Dolores, RP51

Description : Unpaved road with a wall of green dry bushes on either side and a ridge to the east that is sometimes barely visible. So look for it!
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP510
metas.note:
Where : eastern San Juan, around Villa San Agustín, RP510

Description : SSE ridge to the west, with flatness east (sometimes a ridge can be seen very far).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP52
metas.note:
Where : northern Mendoza, north of the capital, RP52

Description : Concrete road, flatness southeast, ridges north and west.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP55 & RN148
metas.note:
Where : eastern San Luis, from Arizona to Villa de Merlo, RP55/RN148

Description : Mostly north to south divided road, with one lane concrete and one lane asphalt, a ridge can be seen east in the northern part. Has drier vegetation than the divided road in Entre Rios.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP60
metas.note:
Where : southern Río Negro, north of Cona Niyeu, RP60

Description : Mongolia-looking road ! Barely constitutes a road. Almost looks as if the driver veered off somewhere.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP61 North of Taco Pozo
metas.note:
Where : western Chaco, northeast of Taco Pozo, RP61

Description : Brown soil with a wall of dry green vegetation on either side. Animal footprints are commonly visible. Beware the N-S section of the road otherwise has a consistent road angle.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RP92
metas.note:
Where : northern Santiago del Estero, south of Monte Quemado, RP92

Description : Very straight north south road, paved, road slightly wet, can be mistaken with the road south of Nueva Esperanza (R2 Santiago del Estero) however the grass on the R2 is of a way brighter green than this one (and the car/copyright is different).
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: RPJ/K
metas.note:
Where : southern Tierra del Fuego, around Puerto Almanza, RPJ/K

Description : Road in between mountains, water south on the southern portion with southern Patagonian forest.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Salta
metas.note:
Description : Salta has a very imposing ridge to the west and dry irregular hills to the east.

You will sometimes see elevation to the north and therefore might confuse it with Catamarca, but Salta is generally more dry-looking.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: San Juan
metas.note:
Description : San Juan will have big mountains to the west and a very flat ridge to the east (sometimes a ridge north is also visible). Vineyards are pretty common.

It is easily possible to confuse it with Mendoza however Mendoza won’t have a ridge to the east.

Moreover, San Juan does a lot of yellow (or red) painted bottom pole paint, which is rarer in Mendoza.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: San Luis
metas.note: Description : San Luis is the only major city with a big ridge to the east or northeast and flatness to the south and west.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Sierra de La Ventana
metas.note:
Where : southwestern Buenos Aires, west of Sierra de La Ventana, RP76

Description : Overcast with a distinct dry, rocky ridge and pines commonly. Possibly even a bit New Zealand-esque to me. The south section is Gen 3 and has pale soil and the ridge is not always visible.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Tucumán
metas.note: Description : San Miguel de Tucumán has a distinct tropical vibe, white stickers on most poles and a ridge west can sometimes be seen.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Ushuaïa
metas.note: Description : Ushuaïa is by far the most distinct town in Argentina, with massive snow-capped mountains to the north.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Villa Pehuenia
metas.note:
Where : western Neuquén, south of Villa Pehuenia

Description : Looks a lot like Chile and has monkey puzzle tree spam commonly.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Volcán Diamante
metas.note:
Where : central Mendoza, west of San Rafael, roads around El Diamante

Description : A very distinct conical volcano which can be seen from very far.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina

metas.name: Volcán Tromen
metas.note:
Where : northern Neuquén, north of Chos Malal, roads around Volcán Tromen

Description : Very distinct volcano and has snow in Gen 4, but the POI is hard to find.
metas.footer: Check the guide for more : A Learnable Argentina
